_comment: SignalLab settings. The server reads this file at start-up; every key can also be
given on the command line, and the command line wins. Changes made in the page are
written back here, so this file is the record of how the app is configured.
mode: 'live' polls MEXC futures and keeps a record; 'replay' walks the local archive.
symbols: an explicit list (BTCUSDT or BTC_USDT both work). Leave it empty to scan
the auto_top most liquid USDT contracts - that is how 100+ instruments fit
in a file instead of a 100-argument command line.
auto_top: how many of the most-liquid contracts to scan when 'symbols' is empty.
timeframes: any of 1m 3m 5m 10m 15m 30m 45m 1h 2h 3h 4h. Measured on 2024-2026
(BTCUSDT + ETHUSDT, 5 bp round trip, 1:4, non-overlapping, see
results/timeframes.json), expectancy after fees per trade was:
The three positive clocks are on by default. 1m-30m are not on because
the fee is a large fraction of R there and every stop/target pair we
measured lost money; enabling them adds signals that lose the fee.
scan_bars: on start-up, look back this many closed bars per timeframe so signals
that are still in play appear immediately instead of hours later.
poll_seconds: how often every instrument is re-read. Lower = faster signals, more
requests; 12 workers fetch ~600 candles sets per poll.
workers: parallel exchange requests. Raise slowly; MEXC throttles.
fee_bp: round-trip cost in basis points of price (taker 2 bp x2 + 1 bp slippage).
cut_override: null = use each timeframe's measured probability cut (geoms.json).
risk_per_trade_pct / equity_usd: used to print position size on every card.
max_candidates: how many actionable setups the page shows at once.
